title: Mlai mid domain data leakage
question: What is data leakage in a machine learning pipeline, and can you give an example of a subtle way it can creep in?
idealAnswer:
Data leakage happens when information that wouldn't be available at real prediction time ends up influencing the model during training, causing inflated performance that doesn't hold up in production

Example: normalizing or scaling the entire dataset, computing mean and standard deviation, before splitting into train and test, so the test set's statistics leak into training

Example: a feature that's a proxy for the target and only known after the outcome occurs, e.g. using number of follow-up support tickets to predict whether a customer will churn

Example in time-series: using future data points to construct features for a past prediction, e.g. computing a rolling average that includes days after the prediction date

Leakage is dangerous because it's often invisible in offline metrics, the model looks great in evaluation and then fails or underperforms once deployed with real-time data

Guarding against it requires understanding exactly what information would genuinely be available at prediction time in production, feature by feature
